name: Rader prime-length discrete Fourier transform
definition: For prime p, primitive root g modulo p and W=e^(−2πi/p), define a_j=x_(g^j mod p), b_l=W^(g^(−l) mod p); X_(g^(−m) mod p)=x_0+Σ_(j=0)^(p−2)a_j b_((m−j) mod (p−1)), X_0=Σ_(n=0)^(p−1)x_n.
variables: p prime length; g primitive root; j,l,m indices modulo p−1; W primitive pth root of unity
assumptions: Prime p and verified primitive root g; finite complex vector; negative-exponent unnormalized DFT
limitations: Modular permutations and convolution length p−1 introduce overhead; cost depends on convolution implementation and factorization
failure_conditions: Incorrect modular permutation or circular convolution normalization
computation: Permute nonzero indices using g, compute the length-(p−1) circular convolution, add x_0 and scatter outputs; calculate DC separately.

source.citation: Rader, C. M. (1968). Discrete Fourier transforms when the number of data samples is prime. Proceedings of the IEEE 56(6), 1107–1108. https://doi.org/10.1109/PROC.1968.6477

application: General prime-length Fourier transformation; no forecasting benefit claimed.
required_inputs: Finite complex vector of prime length, primitive root and matching convolution convention
incompatible_methods: Composite-length input for this primitive-root permutation
mechanism_note: Multiplicative-group indexing converts a prime-length DFT to a cyclic convolution; the chirp identity is not required. Same DFT output as other DFT algorithms, but a distinct computational reduction. For p=2 the nonzero group has one element; use g=1 or compute directly.

name: Good–Thomas coprime-factor discrete Fourier transform
definition: For N=ab with gcd(a,b)=1, u=b^(-1) mod a, v=a^(-1) mod b, n=(n_1bu+n_2av) mod N, k=(k_1b+k_2a) mod N, X_k=Σ_(n_1=0)^(a−1)Σ_(n_2=0)^(b−1)x_n exp(−2πi(n_1k_1/a+n_2k_2/b)).
variables: a,b coprime integer factors; u,v modular inverses; n_1,k_1 indices modulo a; n_2,k_2 indices modulo b
assumptions: a,b>1 and coprime; finite complex inputs; exact modular indexing; unnormalized negative-exponent transform
limitations: Only coprime factorization permits the stated twiddle-free mapping. Permutation overhead and subtransform cost depend on implementation
failure_conditions: Noncoprime factors or wrong modular inverses
Incorrect output permutation or transform convention
computation: Gather input by the Chinese remainder map, perform length-a and length-b transforms along the two axes, and scatter using the stated output map.

source.citation: Good, I. J. (1958). The interaction algorithm and practical Fourier analysis. JRSS B 20(2), 361–372. https://doi.org/10.1111/j.2517-6161.1958.tb00300.x

application: General composite-length Fourier transformation for coprime factors; no forecast benefit claimed.
required_inputs: Finite complex vector, two coprime factors and modular inverses
mechanism_note: CRT input and dual output indexing eliminate interstage twiddle factors. This is a distinct computational factorization from the radix-two Cooley–Tukey recurrence; coprimality is essential.

name: Goertzel recurrence for an integer DFT bin
variables: N positive integer length; k integer with 0≤k<N; ω bin angular frequency; s recurrence state; i imaginary unit
assumptions: Finite real or complex vector, exact integer bin and negative-exponent unnormalized DFT
limitations: O(N) operations per bin and constant state; repeated evaluation of many bins can be slower than FFT; cancellation and state growth can impair finite-precision accuracy
computation: Advance the two-state recurrence once per sample; compute the complex terminal combination. Repeat independently only for requested bins.

source.citation: MathWorks. goertzel: Discrete-Time Fourier transform with second-order Goertzel algorithm. https://www.mathworks.com/help/signal/ref/goertzel.html

application: General selective Fourier coefficient evaluation; no forecasting benefit claimed.
required_inputs: Finite vector and valid integer frequency bin
incompatible_methods: Uncorrected terminal phase for noninteger bins
mechanism_note: Second-order recurrence evaluates one Fourier coefficient without a full transform. Integer-bin phase follows from e^(−iNω)=1; this is not an FFT butterfly factorization.

name: Orthonormal Walsh–Hadamard transform in natural order
variables: m nonnegative integer; N vector length; H_r Sylvester Hadamard matrix of order r; x,y input and output
assumptions: Finite real or complex vector of power-of-two length; natural Sylvester order and unitary normalization
limitations: Ordering and normalization differ among libraries; non-power-of-two lengths require a separately specified embedding; different basis from sinusoidal and localized wavelet bases
failure_conditions: Length not a power of two without explicit padding convention
computation: Apply sum-and-difference butterflies to pairs at each of m bit positions; divide by √N once. O(N log N) additions and O(N) storage for N>1.
application: General orthogonal transform of finite vectors; no forecasting benefit claimed.
required_inputs: Finite vector of power-of-two length and explicit coefficient ordering
incompatible_methods: Unspecified sequency ordering or implicit padding
mechanism_note: A global binary-character basis, not the localized Haar wavelet or sinusoidal Fourier basis. H_N H_N^T=N I follows by block multiplication. Classified as a feature transformation, not an extra distinct FFT algorithm.
